hits: Conjecture: For n > 0, F(n) is the number of all admissible residue classes for which specific finite subsequences of the Collatz 3n + 1 function consists of n+2 terms. This has been verified for 0 < n < 51. For details see Links. - _Mike Winkler_, Oct 03 2014
Conjecture: for all c such that 2-phi <= c < 2*(2-phi) we have F(n) = floor(phi*a(n-1)+c) for n > 2. - _Gerald McGarvey_, Jul 21 2004
A000045.name: Fibonacci numbers: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1.

hits: Conjecture: For any positive integer n, the polynomial Sum_{k=0..n} a(k)*x^k is irreducible over the field of rational numbers. - _Zhi-Wei Sun_, Mar 23 2013

Conjecture: All the rational numbers Sum_{i=j..k} 1/a(i) with 0 < min{2,k} <= j <= k have pairwise distinct fractional parts. - _Zhi-Wei Sun_, Sep 24 2015 - This was proved by an autonomous AI agent, see the Google Deepmind Lean file. - _Ralf Stephan_, May 25 2026
A000108.name: Catalan numbers: C(n) = binomial(2n,n)/(n+1) = (2n)!/(n!(n+1)!).

hits: Conjecture. Let S(1)={1} and, for n>1, let S(n) be the smallest set containing x+1 and 2x+1 for each element x in S(n-1). Then a(n) is the number of the elements in S(n). (See A122554 for a sequence defined in this way.) - _John W. Layman_, Nov 21 2007 [edited by _Sela Fried_, Feb 18 2026].
A000126.name: A nonlinear binomial sum.

hits: Conjecture: a(n) == 2 (mod n^3) iff n is prime. - _Gary Detlefs_, Mar 22 2013
A000172.name: The Franel number a(n) = Sum_{k = 0..n} binomial(n,k)^3.

hits: Conjecture: a(n) = Sum_{k=1..n} A010052(n*k). - _Velin Yanev_, Jul 04 2021
A000188.name: (1) Number of solutions to x^2 == 0 (mod n). (2) Also square root of largest square dividing n. (3) Also max_{ d divides n } gcd(d, n/d).

hits: Conjecture: a(n) is the number of intersection points of n cevians that cut a triangle into the maximum number of pieces (see A007980). - _Anton Zakharov_, May 07 2017
A000212.name: a(n) = floor(n^2/3).

hits: Conjecture: For n > 0, there is always a prime between A000217(n) and A000217(n+1). Sequence A065383 has the first 1000 of these primes. - _Ivan N. Ianakiev_, Mar 11 2013

Conjecture: the sequence is the genus/deficiency of the sinusoidal spirals of index n which are algebraic curves. The value 0 corresponds to the case of the Bernoulli Lemniscate n=2. So the formula conjectured is (n-1)(n-2)/2. - _Wolfgang Tintemann_, Aug 02 2015

Conjecture: Let m be any positive integer. Then, for each n = 1,2,3,... the set {Sum_{k=s..t} 1/k^m: 1 <= s <= t <= n} has cardinality a(n) = n*(n+1)/2; in other words, all the sums Sum_{k=s..t} 1/k^m with 1 <= s <= t are pairwise distinct. (I have checked this conjecture via a computer and found no counterexample.) - _Zhi-Wei Sun_, Sep 09 2015
A000217.name: Triangular numbers: a(n) = binomial(n+1,2) = n*(n+1)/2 = 0 + 1 + 2 + ... + n.

hits: Conjecture: Every integer can be represented as a sum of three generalized square pyramidal numbers. A related conjecture is given in A336205 corresponding to pentagonal case. A stronger version of these conjectures is that every integer can be expressed as a sum of three generalized r-gonal pyramidal numbers for all r >= 3. In here "generalized" means negative indices are included. - _Altug Alkan_, Jul 30 2020
A000330.name: Square pyramidal numbers: a(n) = 0^2 + 1^2 + 2^2 + ... + n^2 = n*(n+1)*(2*n+1)/6.

hits: Conjecture: a(n+3) = Sum_{0 <= k, L, m <= n; k + L + m <= n} k*L*m. - _Ralf Stephan_, May 06 2005
A000579.name: Figurate numbers or binomial coefficients C(n,6).

hits: Conjecture: Let f(n) = (x+y)^a(n), and g(n) = x^a(n), and h(n) = (x+y)^A046660(n) * y^A001221(n) with x, y complex numbers and 0^0 = 1. Then f(n) = Sum_{d|n} g(d)*h(n/d). This is proved for x = 1-y (see Dressler and van de Lune link). - _Werner Schulte_, Feb 10 2018
A001222.name: Number of prime divisors of n counted with multiplicity (also called big omega of n, bigomega(n) or Omega(n)).

hits: Conjecture: a(n) = Sum_{k=2^n..2^(n+1)-1} A178244(k). - _Mikhail Kurkov_, Feb 20 2021
A001700.name: a(n) = binomial(2*n+1, n+1): number of ways to put n+1 indistinguishable balls into n+1 distinguishable boxes = number of (n+1)-st degree monomials in n+1 variables = number of monotone maps from 1..n+1 to 1..n+1.

hits: Conjecture: if p is an odd prime then a((p^3-1)/2) = p * a((p^2-1)/2). Because otherwise a((p^3-1)/2) < p * a((p^2-1)/2) iff a((p^3-1)/2) = a((p-1)/2) for a prime p. Equivalently p^3 divides 2^(p-1)-1, but no such prime p is known. - _Thomas Ordowski_, Feb 10 2014
A002326.name: Multiplicative order of 2 mod 2n+1.

hits: Conjecture: All the rational numbers Sum_{i=j..k} 1/a(i) with 0 < min{2,k} <= j <= k have pairwise distinct fractional parts. - _Zhi-Wei Sun_, Sep 24 2015
A002618.name: a(n) = n*phi(n).

hits: Conjecture: Sum_{k>=0} a(k) / exp(k*Pi) = Pi^(1/2)/Gamma(3/4)^2 = A175574. - _Simon Plouffe_, Sep 09 2025
A004018.name: Theta series of square lattice (or number of ways of writing n as a sum of 2 squares). Often denoted by r(n) or r_2(n).

hits: Conjecture: For each n=1,2,3,... the polynomial a_n(x) = Sum_{k=0..n} C(n,k)^2*C(n+k,k)*x^k is irreducible over the field of rational numbers. - _Zhi-Wei Sun_, Mar 21 2013
Conjecture: a(n)^2 = Sum_{k = 0..n} (-1)^(n+k)*binomial(n, k)*binomial(n+k, k)*A143007(n, k). - _Peter Bala_, Jul 08 2024
A005258.name: Apéry numbers: a(n) = Sum_{k=0..n} binomial(n,k)^2 * binomial(n+k,k).

hits: Conjecture: For each n = 1,2,3,... the Apéry polynomial A_n(x) = Sum_{k = 0..n} binomial(n,k)^2*binomial(n+k,k)^2*x^k is irreducible over the field of rational numbers. - _Zhi-Wei Sun_, Mar 21 2013
A005259.name: Apery (Apéry) numbers: Sum_{k=0..n} (binomial(n,k)*binomial(n+k,k))^2.

hits: Conjecture: a(n)==3 (mod n^3) iff n is an odd prime. - _Gary Detlefs_, Mar 23 2013. The congruence a(p) = binomial(3*p,p) = 3 (mod p^3) for odd prime p is a known generalization of Wolstenholme's theorem. See Mestrovic, Section 6, equation 35. - _Peter Bala_, Dec 28 2014
A005809.name: a(n) = binomial(3n,n).

hits: Conjecture: If n is such that 2^n-1 is in A066175 then a(n) is a triangular number. - _Ivan N. Ianakiev_, Aug 26 2013

Conjecture: Every multiply-perfect number is practical (A005153). I've verified this conjecture for the first 5261 terms with abundancy > 2 using Achim Flammenkamp's data. The even perfect numbers are easily shown to be practical, but every practical number > 1 is even, so a weak form says every even multiply-perfect number is practical. - _Jaycob Coleman_, Oct 15 2013

The only terms m > 1 of this sequence that are not in A145551 are m for which sigma(m)/m is not a divisor of m. Conjecture: after 1, A323653 lists all such m (and no other numbers). - _Antti Karttunen_, Mar 19 2021
A007691.name: Multiply-perfect numbers: n divides sigma(n).

hits: Conjecture: the sequence contains exactly those k such that sigma(k) > k*BigOmega(k). - _Irina Gerasimova_, Jun 08 2013
A008578.name: Prime numbers at the beginning of the 20th century (today 1 is no longer regarded as a prime).

hits: Conjecture: a(n) is the determinant of Redheffer matrix A143104 where T(n, n) = 0. Verified for the first 50 terms. - _Mats Granvik_, Jul 25 2008

Conjecture: Consider the table A051731 and treat 1 as a divisor. Move the value in the lower right corner vertically to a divisor position in the transpose of the table and you will find that the determinant is the Moebius function. The number of permutation matrices that contribute to the Moebius function appears to be A074206. - _Mats Granvik_, Dec 08 2008
A008683.name: Möbius (or Moebius) function mu(n). mu(1) = 1; mu(n) = (-1)^k if n is the product of k different primes; otherwise mu(n) = 0.

hits: Conjecture: Sum_{k>=0} a(k) / exp(k*Pi) = (1/2) * exp(1/24*Pi) * Pi^(1/4) * 2^(5/8) / Gamma(3/4) = A259148. - _Simon Plouffe_, Sep 09 2025
A010815.name: From Euler's Pentagonal Theorem: coefficient of q^n in Product_{m>=1} (1 - q^m).

hits: Conjecture: For n = 2, a(n) is the greatest k such that A123663(k) < A000217(n - 2). - _Peter Kagey_, Nov 18 2016
A011848.name: a(n) = floor(binomial(n, 2)/2).

hits: Conjecture: For any nonnegative integer k and positive integer n, the sum of the k-th powers of the unitary divisors of n is divisible by the sum of the k-th powers of the odd unitary divisors of n (note that this sequence lists the sum of the 0th powers of the unitary divisors of n). - _Ivan N. Ianakiev_, Feb 18 2018

Conjecture: Let b(i; n), n > 0, be multiplicative sequences for some fixed integer i >= 0 with b(i; p^e) = (Sum_{k=1..i+1} A164652(i, k) * e^(k-1)) * (i+2) / (i!) for prime p and e > 0. Then we have Dirichlet generating functions: Sum_{n > 0} b(i; n) / n^s = (zeta(s))^(i+2) / zeta((i+2) * s). Examples for i=0 this sequence, for i=1 A226602, and for i=2 A286779. - _Werner Schulte_, Feb 17 2022
A034444.name: a(n) is the number of unitary divisors of n (d such that d divides n, gcd(d, n/d) = 1).

hits: Conjecture: 2^n-1 is squarefree iff gcd(n,2^n-1)=1. If true, the conjecture would imply that Mersenne numbers (A001348) are squarefree. - _Vladeta Jovovic_, Apr 12 2002. But the conjecture is not true: counterexamples are n = 364 and n = 1755, i.e., gcd(364,2^364-1) = 1 and (2^364-1) mod 1093^2 = 0 and gcd(1755,2^1755-1) = 1 and (2^1755-1) mod 3511^2 = 0, cf. A001220. - _Vladeta Jovovic_, Nov 01 2005. The conjecture is true with assumption that n is not a multiple of A002326((q-1)/2), where q is a Wieferich prime A001220. - _Thomas Ordowski_, Nov 17 2015
A049094.name: Numbers m such that 2^m - 1 is divisible by a square > 1.

hits: Conjecture: a(2^e) = 1 + floor(2^e/(2^4-1)) if e == 0 (mod 4). a(2^e) = 2 + floor(2^e/(2^4-1)) if e == {1,2,3} mod 4. - _R. J. Mathar_, Oct 22 2017
Conjecture: a(p^e) = 1 + floor((p-1)*p^(e+3)/(gcd(p-1,4)*(p^4-1))) for odd primes p. - _R. J. Mathar_, Oct 22 2017
A052273.name: Number of distinct 4th powers mod n.

hits: Conjecture: Let (f(n)), n > 0, be a multiplicative sequence. Then holds:
A069208.name: a(n) = Sum_{ d divides n } phi(n)/phi(d).

hits: Conjecture: a(n) is the number of intervals in a poset closely related to Hochschild lattices. The cardinality of the poset is A001792(n). For example, the total order on 3 elements has 6 intervals. - _F. Chapoton_, Feb 06 2026
A081278.name: Binomial transform of Chebyshev polynomial coefficients A001793.

hits: Conjecture: for n>12 and n>0 modulo 12: a(n)=a(n-12) and a(12*k)=A065331(k)*144.
A081320.name: Largest 3-smooth divisor of n-th Fibonacci number.

hits: Conjecture: a(n) = 2*a(n-1) + A039717(n). - _Benito van der Zander_, Nov 20 2015
A081567.name: Second binomial transform of F(n+1).

A084261.name: A binomial transform of factorial numbers.

hits: Conjecture: a(n) = b(2^(n-1) - 1) for n > 0 with a(0) = 1 where b(n) = b((n - 2^f(n))/2) + b(floor((2n - 2^f(n))/2)) + b(A025480(n-1)) for n > 0 with b(0) = 1 and where f(n) = A007814(n). - _Mikhail Kurkov_, Jan 11 2022
A090365.name: Shifts 1 place left under the INVERT transform of the BINOMIAL transform of this sequence.

hits: Conjecture: Let n = (2^k0)*(p1^k1)*(p2^k2)*...*(pm^km) be the prime factorization of n where p1, p2, ..., pm are distinct primes. Then a(n) is multiplicative and is given by a(n) = f(k0)*g(k1)*g(k2)*...*g(km), where f(0) = 1, f(1) = 2, f(k) = 4(k-1) if k>1 and g(k) = 2k+1 (This has been verified for n = 1-10000.) [Corrected by _Jianing Song_, Mar 24 2019]
A092089.name: Number of odd-length palindromes among the k-tuples of partial quotients of the continued fraction expansions of n/r, r = 1, ..., n.

hits: Conjecture: lim sup_{n -> oo} a(n)/9^log_10(n) = lim_{k -> oo} a(10^k - 2)/9^k = 4/3. - _M. F. Hasler_, Jul 11 2026
A093811.name: Sum of the digital products of the divisors of n.

hits: Conjecture: a(0)=1, a(n+1) = (a(n)*8) XOR a(n), where XOR is the bitwise exclusive-or operator. - _Alex Ratushnyak_, Apr 22 2012
A100311.name: Modulo 2 binomial transform of 8^n.

A101500.name: A Chebyshev transform of the central binomial numbers.

A102318.name: A mean binomial transform of the Catalan numbers.

A102319.name: A mean binomial transform of the central binomial numbers.

A102879.name: A Chebyshev transform of the first kind of the central binomial numbers.

A103769.name: Trinomial transform of central binomial coefficients A001405.

A103821.name: A Whitney transform of the central binomial coefficients A000984.

hits: No more terms < 100000000. Conjecture: sequence is full. - _Jon E. Schoenfield_, Jul 25 2015
A105403.name: Numbers n such that prime(n)-1 and prime(n+1)-1 have the same largest prime factor.

A113409.name: A transform of the central binomial coefficients A001405.

A119967.name: A transform of the central binomial coefficients C(n,floor(n/2)).

hits: Conjecture: Given A054523^k, k = any positive integer, "zero" appears only in the sequence A018391 (k=24).
A128391.name: A054523^24 * A000594.

hits: Conjecture: Given A126988^k, k any positive integer, A128392 is the only sequence in the infinite set with zeros.
A128392.name: A126988^12 * A000594.

hits: Conjecture: denominator of 4/n - 2/n^2. - _Wesley Ivan Hurt_, Jul 11 2016
A129194.name: a(n) = (n/2)^2*(3 - (-1)^n).

hits: Conjecture: The sequence appears to be (1, 7, ...) followed by 4k + 14; k=0,1,2,...; thus: (1, 7, 14, 18, 22, 26, ...).
A131439.name: Inverse binomial transform of A131438 (assuming zero offset in both sequences).

A133158.name: Binomial transform of A126568, second binomial transform of A026641.

hits: Conjecture: rightmost digit of terms is cyclic: (1, 6, 6, 6, ... repeat).
A143132.name: Binomial transform of [1, 5, 15, 35, 70, 0, 0, 0, ...].

hits: Conjecture: Given any sequence with Hankel transform of [1,1,1,...], performing alternate operations: binomial transform followed by INVERT transform, then binomial transform of the last result (repeat); or INVERT transform starting first, will converge upon A006789 and A153197 as a two sequence limit cycle. The conjecture can be extended to any Hankel transform (and their accompanying sequence set): analogous operations will converge upon a Bessel-type sequence and its binomial transform.
A153197.name: Binomial transform of Bessel numbers A006789.

A157021.name: a(n)=sum{k=0..floor(n/2), C(n,2k)*A000108(floor(k/2))}. Inverse binomial transform is aeration of doubled Catalan numbers.

hits: Conjecture: a(n^k) is never of the form x^k, for any integers n > 0, k > 1, x >= 1. This holds at least for squares, cubes, seventh and eleventh powers (see A365808, A365801, A366287 and A366391). - _Antti Karttunen_, Sep 24 2023, Oct 10 2023.
A163511.name: a(0)=1. a(n) = p(A000120(n)) * Product_{m=1..A000120(n)} p(m)^A163510(n,m), where p(m) is the m-th prime.

A166588.name: Partial sums of A097331; binomial transform of A166587.

hits: Conjecture: a(n) = lim_{x->n} f(Pi*x), where f(x) = sin(x)*Sum_{k>0} (cot(x/(2*k))/(2*k) - 1/x). - _Velin Yanev_, Dec 16 2019
A183063.name: Number of even divisors of n.

A186335.name: A transform of the central binomial coefficients.

hits: Conjecture: A175181(n)/A214027(n) = a(n). This says that the zeros appear somewhat uniformly in a period. The second zero in a period is exactly where n divides the first Lucas number, so this relationship is not really surprising.
A214028.name: Entry points for the Pell sequence: smallest k such that n divides A000129(k).

A219314.name: Composition of the inverse binomial transform of Fibonacci numbers and the Catalan transform of Fibonacci numbers.

hits: Conjecture: a(n) = (7 - 2*(-1)^n)*tau(n) - 4*tau(2*n) = 5*tau(n) - (3 + (-1)^n)*tau(2*n), where tau = A000005. - _Velin Yanev_, Dec 17 2019
A228441.name: Expansion of Sum_{k>0} -(-x)^k / (1 + x^k).

hits: Conjecture: a(n) = (8+4^n)*(1-2*n)/8 for n>1, a(1)=-2. [_Bruno Berselli_, Sep 03 2013]
A228767.name: Second bisection of the inverse binomial transform of the rational sequence with e.g.f. (x/2)*(exp(-x)+1)/(exp(x)-1).

A240434.name: Binomial transform of the sum of the first n even squares (A002492).

hits: Conjecture: this is a permutation of the nonnegative numbers. [Proof outline below due to Patrick Devlin and Semeon Artamonov]
A253074.name: Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct numbers such that a(n-1)+a(n) is not prime.

hits: Conjecture: a(2n+1) = 3 followed by period 3: repeat 2, 6, 6.
A257106.name: Denominators of the inverse binomial transform of the Bernoulli numbers with B(1)=2/3.

hits: Conjecture: a(n) equals the GCD of the inradius terms (p^n-1)/2 for all odd primes, i.e. a(n) = GCD_{k=1..oo} (prime(k+1)^n-1)/2.
A297402.name: a(n) = gcd_{k=1..n} (prime(k+1)^n-1)/2.

hits: Conjecture: the second differences are in [-2,2].
A302334.name: A weighted smoothing applied to the primes as a data set: a(n) = floor(A007443(2n-1)/2^(2n-2)), where A007443 is binomial transform of primes.

hits: Conjecture: Every term divides one or more subsequent terms.
A305058.name: Totients t such that the number of divisors of t equals the number of solutions of phi(x) = t.

hits: Conjecture: for n > 1, a(n) = 1 if and only if n is prime.
Conjecture: composite numbers n such that a(n) is squarefree are only the Carmichael numbers A002997. Cf. A309235. - _Thomas Ordowski_, Jul 15 2019
Conjecture: for k > 0, a(2k+1) = (2k+1)^2 iff 2k+1 is in A121707.
A309132.name: a(n) is the denominator of F(n) = A027641(n-1)/n + A027642(n-1)/n^2.

hits: Conjecture: Let k be some fixed integer and a_k(n) = A005361(n) * k^A001221(n) for n > 0 with 0^0 = 1. Then a_k(n) is multiplicative with a_k(p^e) = k*e for prime p and e > 0. For k = 0 see A000007 (offset 1), for k = 1 see A005361, for k = 2 see this sequence, for k = 3 see A226602 (offset 1), and for k = 4 see A322328.
A322327.name: a(n) = A005361(n) * A034444(n).

hits: Conjecture: a(n) = n! * Product_{p <= n} p^min(0, v_p(H'(n))), where the product ranges over primes p, H'(n) = Sum_{k=1..n} (-1)^(k+1)/k, and v_p(r) is the p-adic valuation of rational r (checked for n < 1100).
A334958.name: GCD of consecutive terms of the factorial times the alternating harmonic series.

hits: Conjecture: a(n) is the smallest prime p such that the number of distinct values of the ratio T(p, k) = (number of nonnegative m < p such that m^k == m (mod p))/(number of nonnegative m < p such that -m^k == m (mod p)) is equal to n for some 0 <= k <= floor((p + 2)/3).
A340281.name: a(n) is the smallest prime p such that the number of distinct values of the ratio (number of nonnegative m < p such that m^k == m (mod p))/(number of nonnegative m < p such that -m^k == m (mod p)) is equal to n for some nonnegative k.

hits: Conjecture: this sequence contains odd prime numbers A065091, but does not contain Carmichael numbers A002997.
Conjecture: Let v(n) = A007814(n) be the 2-adic valuation of n. Define
A346669.name: Numbers r such that the number of nonnegative m < r such that m^k == m (mod r) is equal to k*(the number of nonnegative m < r such that -m^k == m (mod r)), where k = 2^A007814(r-1) + 1.

hits: Conjecture: Let f be an arbitrary arithmetic function. Define for n > 0 the sequence a(f; n) = Sum_{i=1..n, k=1..n} f(gcd(1 + (i-1) * (k-1),n)); then a(f; n) = dc(A000290(n), A000010(n) * dc(A008683(n), f(n)) where dc(x, y) is Dirichlet convolution of x and y; if f is multiplicative, then a(f; n) is multiplicative; row sums of this triangle use f(n) = n (see formula section).
Conjecture: Row sums equal Dirichlet convolution of A000290 and A127473.
A347293.name: Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) = Sum_{i=1..n} gcd(1 + (i-1) * (k-1),n) for 1 <= k <= n.

hits: Conjecture: Let f be an arbitrary arithmetic function. Define for n > 0 the sequence a(f; n) = Sum_{i=1..n, k=1..n} f(gcd(i,n)/gcd(gcd(i,k),n)); a(f; n) equals Dirichlet convolution of f(n)*A000010(n) and A057660(n); if f is multiplicative, then a(f; n) is multiplicative; row sums of this triangle use f(n) = n (see formula section).
Conjecture: Row sums equal Dirichlet convolution of A002618 and A057660.
A350900.name: Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) = Sum_{i=1..n} gcd(i,n) / gcd(gcd(i,k),n) for 1 <= k <= n.

hits: Conjecture: a(n) = Sum_{k=1..n} gcd(k, n) * lambda(gcd(k, n)) for n > 0.
A358272.name: Multiplicative sequence with a(p^e) = (-1)^e * p^(2*floor(e/2)) for prime p and e >= 0.

hits: Conjecture: a(n) = Sum_{k=1..n} gcd(k, n) * A076479(gcd(k, n)) for n > 0.
A358319.name: Multiplicative sequence a(n) with a(p^e) = ((p-2) - (p-1) * e) * p^(e-1) for prime p and e > 0.

A370526.name: Square array read by descending antidiagonals: Define function b(i,n,k) where b(0,n,k) = n, b(1,n,k) = k, b(i,n,k) = A038502(b(i-1,n,k) + b(i-2,n,k)). T(n,k) is the number of steps until reaching the cyclic part of {b(i,n,k)}, or -1 if no cycle exists.

A374464.name: Numbers k such that the odd parts of k and sigma(A003961(k)) are equal, where A003961 is fully multiplicative function with a(prime(i)) = prime(i+1), and sigma is the sum of divisors function.

hits: Conjecture: a(n) = Sum_{i=1..n} gcd(i, n) * gcd(i+1, n).
A384531.name: Multiplicative sequence a(n) with a(p^e) = ((2*e+1) * p - 2*e) * p^(e-1) for prime p and e >= 0.

hits: Conjecture: this sequence is a permutation of the positive integers.
A387731.name: a(n) = n if n <= 3; thereafter a(n) is either the greatest number k < a(n-1) not already used such that gcd(k, a(n-1)) = 1 and gcd(k, a(n-2)) > 1, or if no such k exists then a(n) is the smallest number k > a(n-1) not already used such that gcd(k, a(n-1)) = 1 and gcd(k, a(n-2)) > 1.

hits: Conjecture: Every even number occurs infinitely many times.
A393131.name: a(n) = EulerPhi(2*n+1)/A329726(n); index of witnesses for Solovay-Strassen primality test of 2*n+1 as a subgroup of (Z/(2*n+1)Z)*.
